title: Study guidance
description: Evidence-informed routines for learning proof-aware, computational mathematics.
page_type: resource
---

## Prefer retrieval to rereading

Close the lesson and reconstruct a definition, proof outline, graph, or method.
Then compare. The difference between your reconstruction and the source is
useful evidence for the next study session.

## Keep an error log

For each consequential error, record the prompt, your reasoning, the first
invalid step, the underlying misconception, and a new problem that tests the
same idea. Do not record only the correct answer.

## Interleave after initial learning

Blocked practice helps you learn a new method. Mixed practice teaches you to
choose among methods. Use both, in that order, and revisit material over days
rather than compressing all practice into one sitting.
